manifest.limitations: Development study across 12 SBI method families; saved sample files are not retrained model checkpoints.

spec.name: Comprehensive SBI method guide & validation workflow study
spec.representation: 28 reported daily infections divided by 100 (or 6 epidemiological summaries for summary-based estimators)
spec.shift: 25% reporting instead of 50%; no inference model or prior changes

sir_model_guide.title: Compartmental SIR Epidemic Model in Simulation-Based Inference Papers
sir_model_guide.overview: Almost every benchmark paper in modern simulation-based inference (Lueckmann et al. 2021 sbibm; Papamakarios et al. 2019 SNLE; Greenberg et al. 2019 APT/SNPE-C; Radev et al. 2020 BayesFlow; Toni et al. 2009 ABC-SMC; Ward et al. 2022 RNPE; Kelly et al. 2024 RSNL) uses the compartmental Susceptible–Infectious–Recovered (SIR) model. Its nonlinear feedback loop (S_t * I_t / N) creates a sharp epidemic threshold around R_0 = beta / gamma = 1, while partial and noisy case reporting makes the likelihood p(y_{1:T} | beta, gamma) intractable over latent infection trajectories.

compartments.name: Susceptible
compartments.role: Individuals at risk of contracting infection upon infectious contact (rate beta * I_t / N).

compartments.name: Infectious
compartments.role: Actively infectious individuals transmitting at contact rate beta and recovering at rate gamma.

compartments.name: Recovered / Removed
compartments.role: Permanently immune/removed individuals; population is closed: S_t + I_t + R_t = N = 500.

compartments.name: Reported Daily Incidence
compartments.role: Observed daily case counts after Binomial reporting with probability rho = 0.50 (matched) or rho = 0.25 (shifted).

parameters.name: transmission_rate
parameters.meaning: Effective infectious contact rate per infectious individual per day.

parameters.name: recovery_rate
parameters.meaning: Daily recovery/removal rate; implies mean infectious period D = 1 / gamma in [4.0, 12.5] days.

parameters.name: basic_reproduction_number
parameters.meaning: Expected secondary infections per index case in a fully susceptible population. Epidemic waves occur when R_0 > 1; herd-immunity peak occurs near S* = N / R_0.

parameters.name: reporting_fraction
parameters.meaning: Observation probability per true new infection Delta I_t. Halving rho from 0.50 to 0.25 halves scale summaries (attack rate, peak) while leaving timing/shape summaries invariant.

formulations_in_papers.name: 1. Deterministic Kermack–McKendrick ODE SIR + Binomial/Poisson Observation
formulations_in_papers.papers: Lueckmann et al. (2021) sbibm; Papamakarios et al. (2019); Greenberg et al. (2019); Radev et al. (2020); Deistler et al. (2022); Linhart et al. (2023)
formulations_in_papers.equations: dS/dt = -beta * S * I / N,   dI/dt = beta * S * I / N - gamma * I,   dR/dt = gamma * I;   Y_t ~ Binomial(I(t) or -Delta S_t, rho)
formulations_in_papers.how_used_here: Implemented in study.sir_ode() via 4th-order Runge–Kutta and plotted alongside the stochastic chain-binomial trajectories in both the SIR model explainer and live posterior predictive checks.

formulations_in_papers.name: 2. Discrete-Time Stochastic Chain-Binomial (Reed–Frost / Markov) SIR + Binomial Reporting
formulations_in_papers.papers: Toni et al. (2009); Beaumont et al. (2009); McKinley et al. (2009); Wieland et al. (2026)
formulations_in_papers.equations: Delta I_t ~ Binomial(S_{t-1}, 1 - exp(-beta * I_{t-1} / N)),   Delta R_t ~ Binomial(I_{t-1}, 1 - exp(-gamma)),   S_t = S_{t-1} - Delta I_t,   I_t = I_{t-1} + Delta I_t - Delta R_t,   R_t = R_{t-1} + Delta R_t,   Y_t ~ Binomial(Delta I_t, rho)
formulations_in_papers.how_used_here: Primary generative simulator in experiment/workbench/study.py (latent & sir_compartments) and experiment/bundle/simulator.py. Captures both intrinsic demographic stochasticity (wave timing jitter and early fade-outs) and extrinsic binomial case-reporting noise.

formulations_in_papers.name: 3. Continuous-Time Stochastic-Rate SDE SIR with Time-Varying R_0(t) & Weekend Reporting Lag
formulations_in_papers.papers: Ward et al. (2022) RNPE (rnpe_sir.jl); Kelly et al. (2024) RSNL (rsnl_sir.py)
formulations_in_papers.equations: dR_0(t) = eta * (beta/gamma - R_0(t)) dt + sigma * sqrt(R_0(t)) dW_t;   misspecified observation applies a 50% weekend reporting drop (days 6, 7 mod 7) recouped by 1.5x on Monday (day 1 mod 7).
formulations_in_papers.how_used_here: Audited statically in experiment/workbench/source_audit.py against pinned upstream files (rnpe_sir.jl and rsnl_sir.py). Exposes paper-vs-code drift in rsnl_sir.py where sim_sir defines dI_dt using fixed beta while evolving an uncoupled R_0(t) SDE and is never invoked by run_rsnl.py.

summary_equations.name: attack_rate
summary_equations.epidemiological_meaning: Observed cumulative fraction of the population infected over the 28-day window.

summary_equations.name: peak_incidence
summary_equations.epidemiological_meaning: Height of the epidemic curve peak relative to population N = 500.

summary_equations.name: early_incidence
summary_equations.epidemiological_meaning: First-week cumulative reported cases governing initial exponential takeoff.

summary_equations.name: mean_timing
summary_equations.epidemiological_meaning: Normalized center-of-mass day of the epidemic wave in [0, 1].

summary_equations.name: wave_dispersion
summary_equations.epidemiological_meaning: Temporal width/duration of the epidemic wave governed by R_0 and 1/gamma.

summary_equations.name: growth_log_ratio
summary_equations.epidemiological_meaning: Log ratio of early (days 1–10) to late (days 11–28) cases measuring wave speed.

execution_audit.title: Execution Audit: How Every Model & Check Was Run (or If Run)
execution_audit.summary: This workbench combines (1) real PyTorch neural estimators trained via the sbi library (v0.27.0), (2) hybrid sbi neural networks paired with shared-pool Round-2 selection or vectorized Metropolis–Hastings MCMC, (3) self-contained NumPy/scikit-learn reference-table and surrogate implementations operating on the shared 2,048-simulation bank, (4) static AST source audits of external paper repositories that were NOT executed, and (5) live on-demand browser sub-processes for posterior predictive SIR simulation and checkpoint replay.

tiers.badge: Tier 1 · Real sbi PyTorch Neural Nets (Run Offline)
tiers.was_run: YES — Trained & evaluated in Python (sbi 0.27.0 / PyTorch 2.15.0)
tiers.how_run: Trained as genuine neural networks in PyTorch via sbi.inference.{FMPE, NPE, NPSE, EnsemblePosterior} on CPU using the 2,048-simulation training bank (input: 28 daily counts divided by 100). Posterior draws [128 draws x 128 datasets x 2 params] were sampled for both matched (50%) and shifted (25%) validation banks and saved to prepared-20261031/<METHOD>-<SEED>.npz. In addition, the single-parameter FMPE bundle saves its full neural checkpoint in experiment/bundle/posterior.pt.

tiers.badge: Tier 2 · Real sbi Neural Nets + Pool Selection / Batched MCMC (Run Offline)
tiers.was_run: YES — Trained via sbi PyTorch nets with tractable benchmark sampling
tiers.how_run: TSNPE trains a real sbi RestrictionEstimator + Round-1 NPE(nsf) on 512 simulations, then selects 512 Round-2 simulations from the remaining 1,536 training pool inside the truncated support (rather than running 128 separate simulator loops) and trains Round-2 NPE(nsf). NLE trains a real sbi NLE(maf) likelihood flow and BNRE trains a real sbi BNRE(mlp) ratio classifier on the 6 standardized summaries; to evaluate all 128 validation datasets rapidly, both use a custom vectorized 1,024-grid importance resampler followed by 16-step random-walk Metropolis–Hastings MCMC (sample_potential_mcmc) instead of sequential per-dataset Pyro MCMC.

tiers.badge: Tier 3 · Shared-Bank Python Reference-Table & Surrogate Implementations (Run Offline)
tiers.was_run: YES — Run in Python on the shared 2,048 bank (no external packages)
tiers.how_run: Implemented directly in experiment/workbench/study.py over the 6 standardized summaries of the shared 2,048 training bank: ABC_Reject selects the top-128 Euclidean neighbors; ABC_SMC runs 3 adaptive tolerance rounds (quantiles 0.25 -> 0.12 -> 0.0625) by reweighting the fixed 2,048 bank rather than calling the simulator anew; BSL partitions the prior into an 8x8 grid with shrinkage Gaussian covariances; BOLFI_GP fits a scikit-learn Matern-3/2 GaussianProcessRegressor on 256 simulations; RNPE_Robust evaluates an analytical Gaussian-spike / Cauchy-slab mixture over summary discrepancies (NOT the external danielward27/rnpe package); and GenBayes_Scoring applies Huberized loss importance tempering (learning rate w = 0.65).

tiers.badge: Tier 4 · External Paper Repositories (danielward27/rnpe & RyanJafefKelly/rsnl) — NOT RUN
tiers.was_run: NO — External Julia/Python/JAX repositories were NOT executed; audited statically only
tiers.how_run: Neither external paper repository is installed or executed (Kelly et al. 2024 report ~24.3 hours runtime for RSNL on SIR). Instead, pinned source files (experiment/workbench/paper_evidence/rnpe_sir.jl and rsnl_sir.py) are verified by SHA-256 and inspected via Python AST analysis in experiment/workbench/source_audit.py.

tiers.badge: Tier 5 · Offline Prepared Artifacts vs Live Browser Execution
tiers.was_run: HYBRID — 18 posterior .npz files pre-computed offline; 3 verification endpoints run live
tiers.how_run: The 18 two-parameter benchmark runs in prepared-20261031/ store pre-computed posterior draws (.npz) and metrics (results.json), not saved neural weights. When you click in the browser: (1) /api/predictive loads the fixed 128 posterior draws for dataset 0 and runs 128 fresh stochastic SIR simulations + deterministic ODE curves live; (2) /api/source-audit runs AST & regex checks on rsnl_sir.py and rnpe_sir.jl live; and (3) /api/replay loads experiment/bundle/posterior.pt and draws 2,000 fresh posterior samples live from the 1-parameter FMPE flow.

ABC_Reject.label: Rejection ABC
ABC_Reject.best_suited: Prototyping; few parameters; reusing a reference table of simulations for several datasets
ABC_Reject.limitations: Cost grows quickly with summary dimension; non-zero tolerance inflates the posterior; needs informative summaries
ABC_Reject.key_refs: Tavaré et al. (1997); Beaumont et al. (2002)
ABC_Reject.how_run: Run offline in Python on the shared 2,048-simulation training bank. Computes Euclidean distance across the 6 standardized summaries z_tr and retains the top 128 closest simulations (6.25% acceptance quantile) for each of the 128 validation datasets, with small Gaussian tie-breaking jitter N(0, [0.002, 0.001]).
ABC_Reject.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/ABC_Reject-711.npz.

ABC_SMC.label: ABC-SMC
ABC_SMC.best_suited: Low-dimensional compartmental models with cheap simulators; established in epidemiology
ABC_SMC.limitations: Rerun per dataset; sensitive to distance, tolerance schedule and perturbation kernel
ABC_SMC.key_refs: Toni et al. (2009); Beaumont et al. (2009)
ABC_SMC.how_run: Run offline in Python via a 3-round adaptive quantile schedule (q = 0.25 -> 0.12 -> 0.0625) with Gaussian perturbation kernels and SMC importance weights. Operates over the fixed 2,048 training bank rather than launching new simulator calls per round.
ABC_SMC.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/ABC_SMC-711.npz.

BSL.label: Synthetic Likelihood (BSL)
BSL.representation: 6 epidemiological summaries with shrinkage Gaussian covariance
BSL.best_suited: Noisy or chaotic dynamics with approximately Gaussian summaries
BSL.limitations: Many simulations per MCMC step; Gaussian assumption on summaries
BSL.how_run: Run offline in Python by partitioning the 2D prior box into an 8x8 grid (64 cells), estimating local 6-summary mean and shrinkage covariance (75% local + 25% global + 0.03*I) from the 2,048 training bank, and importance-resampling cells under the Gaussian synthetic likelihood.
BSL.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/BSL-711.npz.

BOLFI_GP.label: BOLFI / GP Surrogate
BOLFI_GP.representation: GP discrepancy surrogate on 6 summaries (256-sim low budget)
BOLFI_GP.best_suited: Expensive simulators such as agent-based models; up to about ten parameters
BOLFI_GP.limitations: GP scaling; posterior accuracy depends on the discrepancy model and acquisition rule
BOLFI_GP.how_run: Run offline in Python using scikit-learn GaussianProcessRegressor (Constant * Matern(nu=1.5) + WhiteKernel) fit to the first 256 simulations of the training bank to emulate the 6 summaries across a 512-point candidate parameter grid (does not use external ELFI).
BOLFI_GP.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/BOLFI_GP-711.npz.

NPE_MAF.label: Amortised NPE · MAF + Embedding
NPE_MAF.representation: 28 daily counts (/100) + joint temporal MLP embedding network
NPE_MAF.best_suited: Repeated or real-time inference; raw time series with embedding networks; cheap calibration checks
NPE_MAF.limitations: Large upfront budget; extrapolates outside the prior predictive; can be overconfident
NPE_MAF.how_run: Trained offline as a real PyTorch Masked Autoregressive Flow (4 transforms, 50 hidden units) jointly with a 2-layer MLP embedding network (Linear(28->32)->ReLU->Linear(32->12)->ReLU) via sbi.inference.NPE on the 2,048 raw 28-day trajectories (/100). Trained for 112 epochs (1.92s CPU) and sampled via get_posterior_samples_on_batch.
NPE_MAF.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/NPE_MAF-711.npz (weights not persisted).

NPE_NSF.label: Amortised NPE · Spline Flow (NSF)
NPE_NSF.best_suited: Repeated or real-time inference; expressive rational-quadratic spline conditionals; cheap calibration checks
NPE_NSF.limitations: Large upfront budget; extrapolates outside the prior predictive; can be overconfident under shift
NPE_NSF.key_refs: Papamakarios & Murray (2016); Durkan et al. (2019); Radev et al. (2020)
NPE_NSF.how_run: Trained offline across 3 independent random seeds (711, 712, 713) as real PyTorch Neural Spline Flows via sbi.inference.NPE(density_estimator="nsf") on the 2,048 raw 28-day trajectories (/100). Trained for 64–97 epochs (~5.8–8.8s CPU per seed) and sampled directly in batches.

NPE_Ensemble.label: Amortised NPE · Deep Ensemble
NPE_Ensemble.representation: EnsemblePosterior across 3 independently seeded NSF flows
NPE_Ensemble.best_suited: Default workflow fallback when single-flow posteriors are overconfident or seed-sensitive
NPE_Ensemble.limitations: Multiplies training and sampling cost by ensemble size; does not fix simulator misspecification
NPE_Ensemble.key_refs: Hermans et al. (2022); Radev et al. (2020)
NPE_Ensemble.execution_badge: Real sbi EnsemblePosterior of 3 NSF flows (offline)
NPE_Ensemble.how_run: Constructed offline using sbi.inference.EnsemblePosterior combining the 3 trained NPE_NSF neural spline flows (seeds 711, 712, 713) with equal mixture weights and sampled across all 128 matched and shifted datasets.
NPE_Ensemble.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/NPE_Ensemble-711.npz.

TSNPE.label: Sequential NPE (APT / TSNPE)
TSNPE.best_suited: A single dataset from an expensive simulator where budget must focus on high-posterior-mass regions
TSNPE.limitations: Retrained per dataset; proposal leakage outside prior support (APT); costly calibration checks
TSNPE.key_refs: Greenberg et al. (2019); Deistler et al. (2022)
TSNPE.execution_badge: Real sbi RestrictionEstimator + NSF pool selection (offline)
TSNPE.how_run: Trains a real sbi RestrictionEstimator classifier + Round-1 NPE(nsf) on the first 512 simulations. To benchmark across 128 validation datasets without 128 separate sequential simulator loops, Round 2 selects 512 simulations from the remaining 1,536 training pool concentrated in the Round-1 high-density support and trains a Round-2 NPE(nsf) flow (total budget 1,024 simulations, 5.15s CPU).
TSNPE.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/TSNPE-711.npz.

NLE.label: Neural Likelihood (NLE / SNLE)
NLE.best_suited: Independent replicates, since the likelihood factorises; changing the prior without retraining
NLE.limitations: MCMC per dataset; density estimation in data space requires low-dimensional summaries
NLE.key_refs: Papamakarios et al. (2019); Boelts et al. (2022)
NLE.execution_badge: Real sbi MAF likelihood net + vectorized MH-MCMC (offline)
NLE.how_run: Trains a real PyTorch conditional Masked Autoregressive Flow likelihood estimator q(z | theta) via sbi.inference.NLE(density_estimator="maf") on the 6 standardized summaries for 100 epochs (2.99s CPU). Posterior sampling across all 128 datasets is executed in parallel via sample_potential_mcmc() (1,024-point importance grid initialization + 16 vectorized random-walk Metropolis–Hastings steps using nle_net.log_prob).
NLE.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/NLE-711.npz.

BNRE.label: Balanced Ratio Estimation (BNRE)
BNRE.best_suited: Discrete parameters; independent replicates; model comparison; balanced loss improves calibration
BNRE.limitations: MCMC per dataset; standard NRE often overconfident at small budgets
BNRE.key_refs: Hermans et al. (2020, 2022); Durkan et al. (2020)
BNRE.execution_badge: Real sbi MLP ratio net + vectorized MH-MCMC (offline)
BNRE.how_run: Trains a real PyTorch MLP likelihood-to-evidence ratio classifier via sbi.inference.BNRE(classifier="mlp") with balanced binary cross-entropy loss on the 6 standardized summaries for 99 epochs (1.13s CPU). Sampled across all 128 datasets via sample_potential_mcmc() using bnre_net.unnormalized_log_ratio(theta, z).
BNRE.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/BNRE-711.npz.

FMPE.label: Flow Matching (FMPE)
FMPE.best_suited: Many parameters; multimodal or strongly correlated posteriors; unconstrained vector fields
FMPE.limitations: Sampling requires solving an ODE; density evaluation is costly
FMPE.key_refs: Wildberger et al. (2023); Sharrock et al. (2024)
FMPE.execution_badge: Real sbi PyTorch net · 3 seeds + live 1D checkpoint
FMPE.how_run: Trained offline across 3 independent random seeds (711, 712, 713) as real PyTorch continuous normalizing flow vector fields via sbi.inference.FMPE on the 2,048 raw 28-day trajectories (/100) for 74–117 epochs (~1.0–1.5s CPU). Additionally, the 1-parameter FMPE model is saved as a full PyTorch checkpoint in experiment/bundle/posterior.pt and can be resampled live in the browser.
FMPE.artifact_note: Saved in prepared-20261031/FMPE-{711,712,713}.npz + live checkpoint experiment/bundle/posterior.pt.

NPSE.label: Score / Diffusion (NPSE)
NPSE.representation: 28 reported daily infections (/100) + variance-preserving SDE score network
NPSE.best_suited: Many parameters; multimodal posteriors; compositional score-based combination across observations
NPSE.limitations: Sampling requires solving a reverse SDE/ODE; no direct closed-form posterior density
NPSE.key_refs: Sharrock et al. (2024); Geffner et al. (2023); Arruda et al. (2026)
NPSE.execution_badge: Real sbi VP-SDE score network + ODE sampler (offline)
NPSE.how_run: Trained offline as a real PyTorch variance-preserving SDE conditional score network via sbi.inference.NPSE(sde_type="vp") on the 2,048 raw 28-day trajectories (/100) for 81 epochs (2.63s CPU), and sampled across all 128 validation datasets via the reverse probability-flow ODE (sample_with="ode", 20.69s CPU).
NPSE.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/NPSE-711.npz.

RNPE_Robust.label: Robust NPE (RNPE Summary Criticism)
RNPE_Robust.best_suited: Suspected misspecification; flagging summaries the simulator cannot reproduce (e.g. shifted reporting)
RNPE_Robust.limitations: MCMC/inference over error adjustment variables per dataset; wider intervals when clean
RNPE_Robust.key_refs: Ward et al. (2022); Kelly et al. (2024)
RNPE_Robust.execution_badge: Shared-bank spike-and-slab Cauchy surrogate (not external repo)
RNPE_Robust.how_run: Run offline in Python as a self-contained spike-and-slab Gaussian N(0, sigma_0^2) + heavy-tailed Cauchy(0, tau_1) summary-criticism model over the 6 standardized summaries of the 2,048 training bank, with prior slab probability adapted via scale-vs-shape regression residuals. Computes both robustified posterior draws and per-summary misspecification probabilities P(z_k = 1 | x_obs). Does NOT execute the external danielward27/rnpe Julia/Python repo.
RNPE_Robust.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] + misspecification probs in prepared-20261031/RNPE_Robust-711.npz.

GenBayes_Scoring.label: Generalised Bayes (Robust Scoring Rule)
GenBayes_Scoring.best_suited: Outliers and observation misspecification when a bounded robust loss can be specified
GenBayes_Scoring.limitations: No universal rule for learning rate w without calibration data; wider intervals under matched data
GenBayes_Scoring.key_refs: Pacchiardi et al. (2024); Gao et al. (2023); Bharti et al. (2026)
GenBayes_Scoring.how_run: Run offline in Python by evaluating a bounded Huber loss across the 6 standardized summaries on the 2,048 training bank (downweighting scale-sensitive dimensions relative to timing/shape dimensions) and importance-resampling under the tempered generalized posterior exp(-w * L_Huber(z_obs, z_sim)) with learning rate w = 0.65.

scale_vs_shape_conflict_z.description: Standardized residual of scale summaries (attack_rate, peak_incidence, early_incidence) given epidemic timing/shape summaries.

results.key_refs: Hermans et al. (2022); Radev et al. (2020)
results.execution_badge: Real sbi EnsemblePosterior of 3 NSF flows (offline)
results.how_run: Constructed offline using sbi.inference.EnsemblePosterior combining the 3 trained NPE_NSF neural spline flows (seeds 711, 712, 713) with equal mixture weights and sampled across all 128 matched and shifted datasets.
results.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/NPE_Ensemble-711.npz.

results.label: Score / Diffusion (NPSE)
results.representation: 28 reported daily infections (/100) + variance-preserving SDE score network
results.best_suited: Many parameters; multimodal posteriors; compositional score-based combination across observations
results.limitations: Sampling requires solving a reverse SDE/ODE; no direct closed-form posterior density
results.key_refs: Sharrock et al. (2024); Geffner et al. (2023); Arruda et al. (2026)
results.execution_badge: Real sbi VP-SDE score network + ODE sampler (offline)
results.how_run: Trained offline as a real PyTorch variance-preserving SDE conditional score network via sbi.inference.NPSE(sde_type="vp") on the 2,048 raw 28-day trajectories (/100) for 81 epochs (2.63s CPU), and sampled across all 128 validation datasets via the reverse probability-flow ODE (sample_with="ode", 20.69s CPU).
results.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/NPSE-711.npz.

results.label: Sequential NPE (APT / TSNPE)
results.best_suited: A single dataset from an expensive simulator where budget must focus on high-posterior-mass regions
results.limitations: Retrained per dataset; proposal leakage outside prior support (APT); costly calibration checks
results.key_refs: Greenberg et al. (2019); Deistler et al. (2022)
results.execution_badge: Real sbi RestrictionEstimator + NSF pool selection (offline)
results.how_run: Trains a real sbi RestrictionEstimator classifier + Round-1 NPE(nsf) on the first 512 simulations. To benchmark across 128 validation datasets without 128 separate sequential simulator loops, Round 2 selects 512 simulations from the remaining 1,536 training pool concentrated in the Round-1 high-density support and trains a Round-2 NPE(nsf) flow (total budget 1,024 simulations, 5.15s CPU).
results.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/TSNPE-711.npz.

results.label: Neural Likelihood (NLE / SNLE)
results.best_suited: Independent replicates, since the likelihood factorises; changing the prior without retraining
results.limitations: MCMC per dataset; density estimation in data space requires low-dimensional summaries
results.key_refs: Papamakarios et al. (2019); Boelts et al. (2022)
results.execution_badge: Real sbi MAF likelihood net + vectorized MH-MCMC (offline)
results.how_run: Trains a real PyTorch conditional Masked Autoregressive Flow likelihood estimator q(z | theta) via sbi.inference.NLE(density_estimator="maf") on the 6 standardized summaries for 100 epochs (2.99s CPU). Posterior sampling across all 128 datasets is executed in parallel via sample_potential_mcmc() (1,024-point importance grid initialization + 16 vectorized random-walk Metropolis–Hastings steps using nle_net.log_prob).
results.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/NLE-711.npz.

results.label: Balanced Ratio Estimation (BNRE)
results.best_suited: Discrete parameters; independent replicates; model comparison; balanced loss improves calibration
results.limitations: MCMC per dataset; standard NRE often overconfident at small budgets
results.key_refs: Hermans et al. (2020, 2022); Durkan et al. (2020)
results.execution_badge: Real sbi MLP ratio net + vectorized MH-MCMC (offline)
results.how_run: Trains a real PyTorch MLP likelihood-to-evidence ratio classifier via sbi.inference.BNRE(classifier="mlp") with balanced binary cross-entropy loss on the 6 standardized summaries for 99 epochs (1.13s CPU). Sampled across all 128 datasets via sample_potential_mcmc() using bnre_net.unnormalized_log_ratio(theta, z).
results.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/BNRE-711.npz.

results.label: Rejection ABC
results.best_suited: Prototyping; few parameters; reusing a reference table of simulations for several datasets
results.limitations: Cost grows quickly with summary dimension; non-zero tolerance inflates the posterior; needs informative summaries
results.key_refs: Tavaré et al. (1997); Beaumont et al. (2002)
results.how_run: Run offline in Python on the shared 2,048-simulation training bank. Computes Euclidean distance across the 6 standardized summaries z_tr and retains the top 128 closest simulations (6.25% acceptance quantile) for each of the 128 validation datasets, with small Gaussian tie-breaking jitter N(0, [0.002, 0.001]).
results.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/ABC_Reject-711.npz.

results.label: ABC-SMC
results.best_suited: Low-dimensional compartmental models with cheap simulators; established in epidemiology
results.limitations: Rerun per dataset; sensitive to distance, tolerance schedule and perturbation kernel
results.key_refs: Toni et al. (2009); Beaumont et al. (2009)
results.how_run: Run offline in Python via a 3-round adaptive quantile schedule (q = 0.25 -> 0.12 -> 0.0625) with Gaussian perturbation kernels and SMC importance weights. Operates over the fixed 2,048 training bank rather than launching new simulator calls per round.
results.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/ABC_SMC-711.npz.

results.label: Synthetic Likelihood (BSL)
results.representation: 6 epidemiological summaries with shrinkage Gaussian covariance
results.best_suited: Noisy or chaotic dynamics with approximately Gaussian summaries
results.limitations: Many simulations per MCMC step; Gaussian assumption on summaries
results.how_run: Run offline in Python by partitioning the 2D prior box into an 8x8 grid (64 cells), estimating local 6-summary mean and shrinkage covariance (75% local + 25% global + 0.03*I) from the 2,048 training bank, and importance-resampling cells under the Gaussian synthetic likelihood.
results.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/BSL-711.npz.

results.label: BOLFI / GP Surrogate
results.representation: GP discrepancy surrogate on 6 summaries (256-sim low budget)
results.best_suited: Expensive simulators such as agent-based models; up to about ten parameters
results.limitations: GP scaling; posterior accuracy depends on the discrepancy model and acquisition rule
results.how_run: Run offline in Python using scikit-learn GaussianProcessRegressor (Constant * Matern(nu=1.5) + WhiteKernel) fit to the first 256 simulations of the training bank to emulate the 6 summaries across a 512-point candidate parameter grid (does not use external ELFI).
results.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] in prepared-20261031/BOLFI_GP-711.npz.

results.label: Robust NPE (RNPE Summary Criticism)
results.best_suited: Suspected misspecification; flagging summaries the simulator cannot reproduce (e.g. shifted reporting)
results.limitations: MCMC/inference over error adjustment variables per dataset; wider intervals when clean
results.key_refs: Ward et al. (2022); Kelly et al. (2024)
results.execution_badge: Shared-bank spike-and-slab Cauchy surrogate (not external repo)
results.how_run: Run offline in Python as a self-contained spike-and-slab Gaussian N(0, sigma_0^2) + heavy-tailed Cauchy(0, tau_1) summary-criticism model over the 6 standardized summaries of the 2,048 training bank, with prior slab probability adapted via scale-vs-shape regression residuals. Computes both robustified posterior draws and per-summary misspecification probabilities P(z_k = 1 | x_obs). Does NOT execute the external danielward27/rnpe Julia/Python repo.
results.artifact_note: Saved as posterior draws [128, 128, 2] + misspecification probs in prepared-20261031/RNPE_Robust-711.npz.

results.label: Generalised Bayes (Robust Scoring Rule)
results.best_suited: Outliers and observation misspecification when a bounded robust loss can be specified
results.limitations: No universal rule for learning rate w without calibration data; wider intervals under matched data
results.key_refs: Pacchiardi et al. (2024); Gao et al. (2023); Bharti et al. (2026)
results.how_run: Run offline in Python by evaluating a bounded Huber loss across the 6 standardized summaries on the 2,048 training bank (downweighting scale-sensitive dimensions relative to timing/shape dimensions) and importance-resampling under the tempered generalized posterior exp(-w * L_Huber(z_obs, z_sim)) with learning rate w = 0.65.

interpretation: Workflow Step (i): Prior predictive & MMD checks detect that 25% shifted reporting creates a strong conflict between scale-sensitive summaries (attack_rate, peak_incidence) and scale-invariant timing/shape summaries (mean_timing, wave_dispersion).

Workflow Step (ii): Amortised estimators (NPE_NSF, NPE_MAF, NPE_Ensemble, FMPE, NPSE) evaluate 128 validation datasets rapidly once trained, but misattribute 25% under-reporting to a lower transmission rate β.

Workflow Step (iii): Global calibration via marginal SBC KS tests and joint TARP curves confirms well-calibrated posteriors under matched 50% reporting, and quantifies joint under-coverage under 25% reporting shift.

Workflow Step (iv): Robust summary-criticism estimators (RNPE_Robust, GenBayes_Scoring) and Rejection ABC flag or downweight corrupted scale summaries and preserve substantially higher β coverage under shifted reporting.
Methods share one training bank and evaluation bank; three seeds for FMPE and NPE_NSF measure training stochasticity, not simulation-bank variation.
